exposure: Delivery mode (normal vaginal, operative vaginal, Cesarean)
cohort: 300 nulliparous women recruited during their first pregnancy
finding: While pelvic floor symptoms differed between women who had vaginal deliveries and Cesarean deliveries from pregnancy up to 8 years postpartum, the differences were not statistically significant at 8 years.
mod_finding: Women with vaginal deliveries experienced an increase in urinary incontinence and vaginal symptoms during pregnancy, while those who had Cesarean deliveries had a decrease in symptoms during pregnancy and lower overall symptom scores at 12 months postpartum.
followup_time: 6 weeks, 6 months, 12 months, and 8 years after first delivery
